text:
kai: Heads up — atlas-liteq canary showing spike in funcall parse failures for multi-turn flows, ~10% vs ~0.8% on fp16. Logs attached.

canary-bot: Canary alert: funcall_parse_failure_rate = 11.2% (5m) for atlas-liteq-canary-v3. https://canary.internal/redwood/atlas-liteq/v3/metrics

maria: Can you paste a minimal failed output example? single example ok.

kai: raw streaming chunks concatenated: `{"action":"update","args":{"id":42,"state":"processing"}\n\n{"action":"notify","args":{"user":"u123","msg":"done"}}` — missing closing brace then a new object starts.

ashley: smells like token cutoff mid-object. atlas-liteq is int8 PTQ with seq packing + streaming. Did quant change EOS handling?

devon: mitigation we use elsewhere: parser rescue heuristics. Example pseudo: find last '}', cut there, try parse; else wrap in [] and parse. Mark repaired-via-heuristic.

benchbot: quick canary numbers (200 multi-turn sessions): fp16 baseline parse_failures=1.1%, atlas-liteq int8=9.7%, repaired_by_heuristic(int8)=2.6%, unrepaired(int8)=7.1%.

sreena: Is this only when streaming is enabled? also check non-stream mirrors and KV cache reuse across turns.

kai: Primarily streaming + kvcache reuse. Non-stream mirroring lower (~2.0% int8). So streaming+cache amplifies it.

maria: Plan: run 2x2 canary matrix: streaming on/off x kvcache reuse on/off, batch {1,4}. Capture raw token boundaries + last-token-id distributions. Run cheap and strict reparsers.

ashley: Add metric: repaired_but_changed_semantics_count. Track checksum of action field before/after repair.

devon: Also dump raw final token ids for failed sessions to S3 for tokenizer bisect. Add repair_confidence score on repaired events.

canary-bot: Canary run 14/50 completed. repaired_by_heuristic=3.2% of failures, unrepaired=9.8% of sessions.

kai: Action items: @maria kick off canary matrix+token-id dumps (sample); @ashley implement structured-output-lint hook (ok/repaired/failed + repair_delta_checksum); @devon add telemetry counters, S3 snapshots, parser-rescue lib opt-in; @sreena run non-stream mirror baseline.

maria: Starting canary runs now, will paste artifacts.

kai: If tokenizer bisect shows PTQ shift, pause atlas-liteq rollout and revert to fp16 for canary traffic.

ashley: Note: avoid aggressive repairs for high-risk actions like delete until semantics checked.

devon: We'll emit repair_confidence so downstream can warn in-app.

kai: tl;dr: int8 canary shows multi-turn streaming parse regressions. short-term: add cheap heuristic rescue + telemetry. medium-term: tokenizer-level bisect to find quantization-induced token shifts.
